findings.rationale: The predictable PID-based materialization path is opened with truncating std::fs::write. A pre-existing file or symlink can therefore be overwritten when a Markdown specification is processed.

Repeated tables and keys are silently accepted and overwritten in the maps. In particular, an ambiguous duplicate [impl] command is treated as valid and the last value is executed by the project chain.

Generation renders AppliedApproval.artifact_digest from target.reviewed_digest, while document check reconstructs it from target.digest. When those intentionally distinct digests differ, a document produced by generate cannot pass the corresponding check.

Monitor::new is preferred even when a versioned trace supplies an explicit validated initial state; from_state is used only if default initialization fails. Valid traces beginning at another permitted state are rejected or replayed from the wrong state.
Several post-baseline I/O, parsing, lowering, and external-mutant loading failures return an error envelope with status 0, allowing CI mutation gates to pass although analysis did not complete.

The command returns nonzero only for signature-invalid. Other non-current statuses produced by approval::evaluate, such as specification or artifact drift, are reported while the process exits successfully.

FileInput records each glossary/evidence digest, but approval rerendering reopens only the recorded paths and never compares their bytes with those digests. The approval can therefore be evaluated against inputs different from the inputs its record claims.

New bounds are applied to the old model only when the bound was explicitly present in old_scope. Adding or removing a declaration-level bound for an existing domain leaves the two models evaluated under different scopes despite the output claiming comparison under the new scope.
A local dataset source declared inside the AI project is converted directly to PathBuf rather than resolved relative to the project file, so evaluation depends on the caller's working directory.

When multiple approval records cover the same requirement, each insert overwrites the previous evaluation. Reordering repeated --approval arguments can therefore change the per-requirement approval displayed by the ledger.
